packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-12 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of the work or author before or during this reading. I have not tried to identify it.

IMPORTANT CAVEAT ON RESOLUTION: the "native" tiles in this packet are only about 1350 px wide for roughly 9 cm of leaf. The script is a small, very heavily abbreviated cursive. At this resolution individual abbreviation strokes do not resolve, and most of the running text can only be read word-shape by word-shape. The display headings and a few clearer spans are reliable; everything marked "?" is a guess at a word-shape and should not be used as a match key on its own. Much of the gap below is a property of the images, but some is surely my effort; a higher-resolution capture would recover a great deal more.

1. LAYOUT SURVEY (image only)

Four faces of two parchment pieces, each lying landscape, labelled in the photographs "A 1" and "B 1", with a 17 cm ruler. Each piece is about 16.5 x 10 cm, with paired holes (sewing/binding reuse) and, on B, slits and losses along the lower edge. Each piece is the upper(?) part of a two-column leaf: text is cut through at the top edge on every face.

- A, first face (image-001 overview; tiles 002-005): two columns, about 15-16 lines each, then blank parchment below (lower half of the piece empty - so this is the foot of the columns, or the text simply ended). Display headings in large textualis inside the columns: "Notandum", "Conclusio responsalis", "Prima" (left column); "Argui/tur" split over two lines (right column). Some words struck through in the right column.
- A, second face (image-006 overview; tiles 007-010): two columns of about 16 lines with display headings touched in red: "Secunda", "[T]ercia", "Quarta" (left column), "Notandum" and again "Notandum" (abbreviated, "nōndū") (right column). Below the columns, across the full width, 12 long lines in a smaller, lighter, more current hand with red-touched paragraph marks: observation - a different module and possibly a different hand; tentative interpretation - an addition filling the lower margin.
- B, first face (image-011 overview; tiles 012-015): two columns, stained dark and abraded. Very large display line "Queritur" plus an abbreviated word, then "Arguitur" three times (left column); "Notan/dum" split over two lines (right column). Several lines in the right column are underlined. Marginal "Nota" in the outer right margin. A diagonal cut and losses at the foot.
- B, second face (image-016 overview; tiles 017-020): two columns. Display headings "Notandum" (with a long-tailed N in the margin), "No/tandum" split, in the left column; "Prima", "Secunda", "Tercia" in the right column; at the foot of the right column a very large line in outlined/hollow capitals "QVERITVR" (partly lost), with "Ar[...]" display below it at the edge. One phrase in the left column is underlined.

Tentative interpretation of the structure (from headings only): a question-format text - "Queritur ..." / "Arguitur ..." / "Notandum ..." / "Conclusio responsalis" / "Prima, Secunda, Tercia, Quarta" - i.e. questions with arguments, notabilia and numbered conclusions or replies. No running titles survive (tops cut). No interlinear glosses seen. Column order and which face is recto are not determinable from the images.

2. AREAS SELECTED / LEFT UNREAD

Selected: every display heading on all four faces and the lines attached to them; B second face left column (the clearest connected prose, about 20 lines); B first face right column upper part (a list); A second face both columns. Left largely unread: the 12 long lines at the foot of A second face (too small to resolve); B first face left column upper lines and right column middle (stain); the cut top line of every column.

3. TRANSCRIPTION (physical lines; line numbers counted from the top of the named tile; expansions in parentheses; "?" follows an uncertain word)
